smeaton_keeper.text: Welcome to Smeaton's Tower! The keepers went up and down ladders between these little rooms, all the way to the lantern. This was the third lighthouse on the Eddystone Rocks.
The first was Henry Winstanley's, all wood and ornament. He was so sure of it he said he'd like to be in it in the worst storm ever. In 1703 he was, and the Great Storm took him and the tower both.
The second was wood again and burned down in 1755. Then John Smeaton came along, a Yorkshireman, and looked at oak trees: wide at the bottom, narrow at the top, and they don't blow over.
He cut granite blocks to lock together like a jigsaw and found a lime that sets under water. Lit in 1759, stood for over a hundred years. The rock gave out before the tower did.
The rooms are tiny. Keepers slept in curved beds. Imagine the gale outside and the whole tower humming. Then imagine the toilet arrangements. Actually, don't.
